scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Both user LANs lost cross-AS connectivity this morning: pc1
(195.11.14.2) cannot reach pc2 (200.1.1.2) and pc2 cannot reach
pc1. Each PC still reaches its own gateway fine. Our NOC checked
router1: its inter-AS interface eth0 shows UP and its config is
unchanged. The partner operator (AS 2) says router2's logs show
the eBGP session dropping. Find what broke.

injection.action: administratively down the inter-AS interface (eth0) on router2

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show eth0 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router2 eth0 (193.10.11.2/24, the inter-AS
  interface toward router1)
Mechanism: router2's eth0 is DOWN, so the physical/L2 path between
  the two ASes is broken at router2's side. router2 immediately
  loses its 193.10.11.0/24 connected route and its BGP route to
  195.11.14.0/24 (nexthop interface gone), and its side of the
  eBGP session drops. Traffic from pc1 toward 200.1.1.0/24 is
  blackholed on the inter-AS segment (nothing listens at
  193.10.11.2 any more), so pc1<->pc2 fails in both directions.
  Note: router1's eth0 still shows UP (the far side of the virtual
  link keeps carrier), and router1 may briefly keep showing the
  session as Established until its hold timer expires -- the
  definitive evidence is router2's eth0 being DOWN.
Localization: router2
Root cause: inter-AS link down at router2 (eth0 administratively
  down)
Fix: `ip link set eth0 up` on router2
scenario.fix_spec:
Bring the inter-AS link back up: on router2 run `ip link set eth0 up`. The
eBGP session re-establishes, the inter-AS prefixes are re-exchanged, and pc1
reaches pc2 normally. router1 needs no change -- it was healthy the whole time.

agent.diagnosis_text:
**Affected component:** The physical/virtual inter-AS interface `eth0` on `router2` is in a hard-DOWN state.

**Mechanism:** With `eth0` down, the kernel removes the directly-connected route for `193.10.11.0/24` from router2's routing table. Router2's BGP daemon therefore has no path to reach its configured eBGP peer at `193.10.11.1` (router1). This triggers the "No path to specified Neighbor" reset, drops the TCP/179 session, and puts the BGP finite state machine back into **Active** (connect-retry). Router2 never re-establishes the session, so it never receives `195.11.14.0/24` from router1. Router1, meanwhile, enters BGP Graceful Restart mode and temporarily holds the stale `200.1.1.0/24` route it learned before the link dropped — so router1's BGP table still looks populated, but the forwarded traffic is black-holed because the physical path is broken. The result is symmetric: `pc1→pc2` gets "Destination Host Unreachable" from router1 (no viable forwarding path), and `pc2→pc1` gets "Destination Net Unreachable" from router2 (no route to `195.11.14.0/24` at all).

**Localization:** `router2`, interface `eth0` (inter-AS link toward router1). `carrier_changes = 2` confirms only startup-level transitions — no active flap process, no ongoing toggling agent. Router1's `eth0` is fully UP and correctly addressed.

**Root cause:** `router2:eth0` is administratively or physically DOWN, severing the only inter-AS link and collapsing the eBGP session.

**Fix:** Bring `router2:eth0` up — `ip link set eth0 up` — to restore the L2/L3 path. Once the interface is UP, the connected route `193.10.11.0/24` will re-appear in the kernel, router2's BGP daemon will successfully open a TCP/179 connection to `193.10.11.1`, the eBGP session will re-establish, and both prefixes will be exchanged, restoring full cross-AS connectivity.
